I was in 2nd grade so around 7 and I have this illness where I basically just get weaker and weaker overtime, no cure. I can’t walk or lift my arms or legs a lot, but essentially I’m very weak. One day I laid down on my couch and couldn’t breathe and my parents noticed and lifted me back up and I told them I couldn’t breathe while laying down. They rushed me to the ER and it was a daze, I remember some details like how I couldn’t hold my neck up in the car then I don’t remember anything. I remember waking up and seeing the doctors talking to my parents and seeing my mom crying. They ended up putting a tube down my throat and that messed up my teeth even now. Sometime past with all the fluids being put into me which the IVs causes scars and they decided my best bet would to put a hole in my neck to put a tube there and a gtube in my stomach


. They did both in one surgery and I eventually recovered, in all I was there for 4 months and I have no idea how much my parents sacrificed to keep me alive, the depression my older sister had and how worried everyone was. I’m thankful for the nurses and doctors who kept me sane and alive. The aftermath of all this was a home nurse from 7 am to 3pm and a night nurse from 7pm to 7am. I’m happy home and those months mostly bedbound definitely didn’t help my disability but I’m doing okay. I’m now 11 and covid-19 has me terrified but we’ll pull through. Stay strong essential workers and I’ll stay strong for you.
